messages:
maria: FYI eu-west3 is seeing attach failures for gpu jobs since ~14:00. lots of nvme io saturation on scratch nodes, attach controller timing out. anyone on call? :frowning:

ashwin: i'm on it. which pools affected? looks like scratchpool-eu-west3 and preemptible-batch-eu-west3 from cluster metrics.

maria: correct. brief kernel log from an affected host:
```
[23456.789012] nvme0n1: io submit returned -11
[23456.789015] FSYNC stall: 400ms (queued=120)
[23457.000100] gattach: error: device attach timeout
```

ben: ouch. modal util% at 99 and avgqu-sz double digits. can you paste `iostat -x 1 2`?

maria: pasted from gnode-11:
```
Device:       rrqm/s wrqm/s   r/s   w/s  rsec/s  wsec/s  avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await  svctm  util
nvme0n1      0.00   0.00   5.0 420.0  200.0  35000.0   82.1    15.8   19.5   3.2   21.8   0.10  99.2
```

olga: sounds like janitor/deep-scrub overlapped with a batch ramp. We recently moved the scrub window earlier in eu-west3 for a rollout.

ashwin: immediate plan: throttle janitor scrubs for eu-west3 and increase attach timeout on controller. low-risk and should buy headroom.

ben: agree. also manually drain a couple of the heaviest preemptible jobs to relieve pressure.

ashwin: kubectl patch to throttle janitor configmap (ready to apply):
```bash
kubectl -n infra patch configmap janitor-config -p '{"data":{"scrub_io_mbps":"40","scrub_parallelism":"1"}}'
```

maria: +1 apply it. i'll start evicting noisy batches.

janitor-bot: [automated] scrub throttling applied in eu-west3 by ashwin: scrub_io_mbps=40, scrub_parallelism=1 at 2025-09-19T14:07:30Z :gear:

ben: also propose temporary scheduler tweak: prefer zone-b nodes for new attach requests if node nvme util > 85%. reduces attach pressure while we investigate.

olga: can we add a detection rule: nvme_util > 90% AND attach_errors > 3/min -> auto-throttle janitor + increase attach_timeout + page oncall? if so we should implement as a short-term playbook.

ben: i'll draft the playbook and include the tradeoffs: throttling scrubs delays wear detection and increases temp file retention (cost), but prevents production attach failures.

ashwin: i've bumped controller attach_timeout from 30s to 60s (rolling deploy will hit in ~3min):
```yaml
controller:
  attach_timeout_sec: "60"
```

maria: after throttle + timeout bump attach backlog cleared in ~5m. still found two nodes reporting soft checksum errors; created ticket to run `nvme smart-log` and mark for follow-up.

sre-oncall: monitoring attaches and nvme util. will escalate if errors re-appear. added short incident note in oncall-runbook.

olga: follow-ups: 1) avoid scrub rollouts during known batch windows; 2) implement scrub placement to avoid hot-stripe nodes; 3) consider incremental scrub chunking so it yields IO more frequently; 4) add auto-detect playbook.

ben: agreed. long-term we should also look at more graceful preemption of janitor work (rate-limit based on per-node avgqu-sz). i'll add to infra backlog.

maria: thanks team. reopening ticket for the two nodes with checksums. keeping this thread for postmortem notes.
